speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a chest skin lesion; please describe how it started, what it looks like, and if it is changing, bleeding, or itchy. To help me understand better, have you noticed any similar spots elsewhere on your body?

speaker: Patient
text: 63-year-old male. The patient reports noticing a skin lesion on his chest 2 months ago, which he believes has increased in size. He denies any associated pain or itching with the lesion. He has a medical history significant for type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and glaucoma.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Basal Cell Carcinoma (BCC) of the chest.

Based on your age, the lesion's location, and the fact that it is growing over two months without symptoms like pain or itching, this presentation is highly suggestive of a non-melanoma skin cancer. Given your history of diabetes and hypercholesterolemia, which can sometimes affect healing and wound assessment, we need to proceed carefully. Would you be willing to have a biopsy to confirm the diagnosis?
